name: Crucible Industries Cerberus-357 'Hellhound'
description:
The Crucible Industries Cerberus-357 is a six-shot double-action revolver chambered in .357 Magnum, featuring three barrels arranged in a triangular cluster. The weapon fires from a single cylinder through whichever barrel is aligned by the rotary barrel selector — the shooter can choose between a standard four-inch barrel, a two-inch barrel for close-quarters work, and a six-inch barrel with a target crown for precision shots. Barrel selection is controlled by a thumb switch on the frame.

The Cerberus is an engineering exercise that somehow became a production weapon. Crucible's design team originally built the triple-barrel prototype as a proof of concept for a military contract that required a single sidearm adaptable to multiple engagement ranges. The contract fell through, but the prototype generated enough interest that Crucible produced a commercial run. The resulting weapon is mechanically complex, heavier than a conventional revolver, and undeniably versatile.

The Hellhound has a cult following among operators who appreciate mechanical ingenuity and don't mind carrying extra weight. The ability to switch between barrels mid-engagement — close range, then stepping back to the precision barrel — provides tactical flexibility that no other revolver offers. Whether that flexibility justifies the weight and complexity is a matter of ongoing debate in firearms forums that generates thousands of comments and zero consensus.
specifications:
caliber: .357 Magnum
effective_range: 15-60 meters (barrel dependent)
rate_of_fire: Double-action revolver
magazine_capacity: 6 rounds (cylinder)
weight: 1.38 kg
tactical_use: A versatile revolver offering three engagement profiles in a single weapon. The two-inch barrel provides maximum maneuverability at close range, the four-inch barrel suits general-purpose use, and the six-inch barrel enables precision shooting. Barrel switching takes approximately one second via the thumb selector. The added weight and mechanical complexity are trade-offs for the unique multi-range capability.
cultural_context: The Hellhound is the firearms equivalent of a conversation starter — nobody sees one without asking about it, and nobody who carries one gets tired of explaining it. In weapon culture, it occupies a space reserved for objects that are simultaneously brilliant and slightly absurd. People either love it or think it's the most over-engineered solution to a problem nobody had.
story_hooks: A Cerberus is found at a crime scene with one barrel recently fired and two clean — but the ballistics match all three barrels at three different crime scenes over three days. Someone is cleaning two barrels after each use.
Crucible Industries announces a four-barrel Cerberus prototype and offers it as a prize in a competition that turns out to be far more dangerous than the entry form suggested.
physical_description: The Cerberus-357 is a brutish, utilitarian revolver with three barrels clustered in a triangular arrangement around a central cylinder, giving it an aggressive, almost organic silhouette. Matte gunmetal finish shows honest wear—scuffs and patina from heavy use—with a reinforced steel frame and a prominent thumb-operated barrel selector switch on the left side. The grip is wrapped in worn synthetic polymer, textured for wet-hand control, and the whole weapon carries the no-nonsense bulk of something designed by engineers who prioritized function over aesthetics.
